summary: This exact one-argument change (moe_align_block_size with 32 experts instead of 256) has already been measured once, in the sibling problem muse_moe_w4a16 (sglang-marlin-path-parity). There it was the only difference from baseline.py, and the judge's SGLang column served as the A/B. Result: decode_1 0.9596 (about 3 us slower, error 0.48 us), every other shape flat, including verify_16/32 at block 48/64. So the stated verify-side mechanism is already refuted and the likely real effect is a small loss at small T. The run is cheap and its per-shape result can be read without companions, so proceed. Re-set the expectations and expect at best a neutral result.
justification: Mechanism: local_ids really are in [-1] U [0,32), so 32 is the true count, and correctness at 32 experts with -1 ids is already established: the sibling's 5 tests passed on the same evaluator (afcead6a...), and SGLang's wrapper accepted 32. The hypothesis expects a gain on verify_16/32 from Marlin walking the host-sized capacity. The sibling result refutes that. At T=128/256 with block 48/64, where the capacity shrink was largest (13056->2528 and 18176->4064 sorted ids), verify_16 came in at 0.9999 and verify_32 at 1.0002. On master's lineage the landed cap means block 16, so the shrink is smaller still: T=128 has 4864->1504 slots and 304->94 m-blocks, T=256 has 5888->2528 slots and 368->158 m-blocks. Marlin plainly works from the device-side num_tokens_post_pad, not the capacity. The one new side effect from the cap: both verify capacities now drop from above SGLang's fused sorted_ids padding threshold (about 4096, unverified) to below it, so each verify shape may lose one separate fill_ launch. That is about 2 us on 437-970 us shapes, under 0.5%, well inside the at-least ±1.5% CI. The expected list is wrong at small T. With 32 experts and numel < 1024 (T <= 127: decode_1/16/32 and verify_1, plus the T=33 test), sgl_kernel switches to moe_align_block_size_small_batch_expert_kernel. That kernel shows up in the sibling profile at bs=32 taking 6.6-6.7 us. The sibling measured decode_1 at 0.9596 (80.2 vs 77.0 us), which is well outside its 0.48 us error. In this layer, decode_1 runs about 171-184 us, so roughly 3 us comes to -1.5 to -2% on the two decode_1 shapes (weight 46+16). That load can land at or just outside the CI on the slow side. decode_16/32 and verify_1 were also 0.988-0.994 in the sibling, inside noise but all on the slow side. Weakest link: the premise that small-T shapes are a 'flat control'. They are the shapes most likely to move, and against the hypothesis, because the expert count picks a different align kernel there. The verify gain itself is close to already disproven.
confounders: marlin-block-m-cap-16 (landed, w13 marlin): block_size_m sets the align capacity (T*8 + E*(bsm-1)) and the m-block count. Under the cap, verify_16/32 run block 16, not 48/64, so the hypothesis's own numbers (18176->4064, 284->64) no longer apply: the real figures are 5888->2528 slots and 368->158 m-blocks at T=256. The cap also moves both verify capacities across the about-4096 fused-padding threshold. Without the cap, the same change was already measured flat (sibling muse_moe_w4a16 at block 48/64), so an ab-revert would re-measure a known null. The cap does not change the small-T path (blocks 8/16 are unchanged), where the real effect, the small-batch kernel selection, sits.

sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8 (landed, router GEMM): it touches the router and routing on the side stream, which produce topk_ids, but not the align path or its buffers. Routing skew only changes which expert counts align sees, not the code path. Not a confounder.
interference: No companion is warranted. (i) An ab-revert of marlin-block-m-cap-16 would test 32 experts at block 48/64, which the sibling problem already measured on the same Marlin/align ops and evaluator: flat on verify_16/32. A verify-side null or gain in this run reads the same with or without that arm. (ii) An ab-tune of the cap gives nothing new: any cap in {8,16} leaves small T untouched, and the verify effect is a fill launch well under resolution. (iii) A control isolating a sub-change does not apply, because the change is a single argument. Its two possible effects (small-batch kernel at numel<1024, smaller capacity and fused padding at T>=128) split cleanly by T and therefore by shape, so per-shape results already attribute them: movement on decode_*/verify_1 is the align kernel switch, movement on verify_16/32 is the capacity and fill. Neither a gain nor a loss is ambiguous without a companion. Scheduling notes: (a) do not stack with moe-align-single-kernel-small-t (in flight). That hypothesis replaces the align op at T<=32 entirely, so if it lands, this change's T<=32 effect disappears and only verify_16/32 remain. Its control (control-capacity-256) already isolates the 32-vs-256 capacity question at T<=32. (b) If this run shows the expected small-T loss with flat verify, the only worthwhile follow-up is a separate hypothesis that applies the 32 count only at T>=128 and keeps 256 below that. Its signal would still be well under 1%.
open_questions: The sgl_kernel small-batch path condition (numel < 1024 and num_experts <= 64, from memory) is not verified against this SGLang commit's source. The sibling profile shows small_batch_expert_kernel at bs=32 with 32 experts, which agrees. T=128 (numel exactly 1024) should stay on the general path, so the implementer should record which align kernel(s) the profile shows for decode_1 and verify_16 on both columns.

Is the fused sorted_ids padding threshold (<=4096) and the (num_experts or num_experts+1)*(bsm-1) sizing correct at this commit? It only decides whether verify_16/32 lose one fill_ launch (about 2 us), which is below resolution either way.

The sibling decode_1 loss (0.9596) did not replicate exactly in its later runs on the same base (align-single-token-ep 0.999, atomic-add 0.969 at bs=1), so its size is uncertain. Expect decode_1 between flat and about -2% in this layer.

The hypothesis's expected list should be corrected before dispatch: decode_1 slower-or-flat (kernel switch), decode_16/32 and verify_1 flat-to-slower, verify_16/32 flat (refuted by the sibling, under 0.5% fill saving at block 16).
